subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw make natural-language suffixes like `reply in thread` or `rit` a built-in cross-channel reply override, and if so which trigger words, default/config behavior, and `replyToMode` precedence are acceptable?
rationale: Current code already has explicit reply tags and static reply modes, but adding hidden inbound suffix parsing creates cross-channel product semantics and possible config surface that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Specify a narrow core directive
options.body: Approve a small suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip all agent-visible body fields while respecting explicit reply policy.

options.title: Keep this prompt or plugin owned
options.body: Leave natural-language phrasing to prompts or plugins and keep core limited to explicit reply tags, typed commands, and configured reply modes.

options.title: Merge into broader thread-routing design
options.body: Fold this into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/28025 if maintainers prefer one broader reply-placement policy over separate suffix syntax.

recommendation.title: Specify a narrow core directive
recommendation.body: Approve a small suffix contract, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and require implementation to strip all agent-visible body fields while respecting explicit reply policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on the inbound finalizer, reply-threading policy, and directive parser surfaces that would own the product-shape decision.
